Stated Claim / Post Context:
Melat Kiros becomes the first Gen Z woman elected to Congress

=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Melat Kiros becomes the first Gen Z woman elected to Congress ===

[Source 1 — www.kuow.org (Bias: Independent / Unrated)] (URL: https://www.kuow.org/npr-news/2026-11-03/melat-kiros-becomes-the-first-gen-z-woman-elected-to-congress):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Melat Kiros becomes the first Gen Z woman elected to Congress

The 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant was one of several candidates to win with backing from the Democratic Socialists of America or its local chapters.

Actual Article Body:
Midterms coverage: Live results | What to know | Stories around the country
Stay connected:  NPR Politics Podcast | NPR Politics newsletter | NPR app

Democratic socialist Melat Kiros has won the race to represent Colorado's 1st Congressional District in the House, according to a race call by The Associated Press, marking the first time a Gen Z woman will serve in Congress.

Kiros, a 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant and lawyer, cruised to victory Tuesday night in the reliably blue district, which includes most of Denver.

The win comes just months after she handily defeated 15-term incumbent Diana DeGette in the state's Democratic primary, a high-profile party upset where voter frustration with leaders in Washington, D.C., and calls for political change were at the forefront.

Loading...

Kiros is one of several winning House candidates on Tuesday who were endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America or its local chapters.

Many touted a shared core platform: championing issues aimed at expanding the social safety net for working Americans through policies like Medicare for All and universal childcare. They also advocated for more divisive changes, such as abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

Kiros' fierce criticism of Israel and the war in Gaza became a source of controversy on the campaign trail, sparking blowback from the independent candidate in her race, Shimon Blau, who accused her of espousing antisemitic rhetoric. Kiros has pushed back on that, saying her criticism rests with the state of Israel rather than the Jewish people.

Though the average age of a lawmaker in Congress has gotten younger in recent years, being a Gen Z member of Congress remains a rarity. Kiros will arrive on Capitol Hill at a moment when Democrats continue to confront calls from many of their voters for generational change.

In an interview with NPR in February, she spoke about the role of age in her race, arguing that many of her policy positions appeal to young voters in particular.

"Young people understand that we are in the fight of our lives," she said. "We need to have leaders that are going to be fighting for the kind of bold policies that actually get something done, and they're refusing to settle or wait for our turn or ask for permission."

Currently, just one sitting member of Congress is under the age of 30, Florida Democrat Maxwell Frost, who became the first Gen Zer elected to the House in 2022.

Copyright 2026 NPR

Woman, 24, dies in NY Marathon as father reveals she had rare condition

Rachel Apa, 24, dies in Central Park just 3km from the New York Marathon finish line after her father reveals she had a rare condition.

Actual Article Body:

TOK PISIN

Topic:Marathon

Rachel Apa, 24, died after suffering a rare condition during the New York Marathon. (Supplied)

Rachel Apa, a 24-year-old from Pennsylvania, died just 3 kilometres from the finish line of the New York Marathon.

Apa's father said she had rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition in which muscles can break down during exertion.

The city medical examiner's office said it was investigating the cause of Apa's death.

A young Pennsylvania woman running the New York City Marathon for the first time to raise money for charity collapsed in Central Park, just over 3 kilometres from the finish line, and later died.

Rachel Apa, 24, of Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, was approaching the finish line in last weekend's event when she collapsed, according to the New York Police Department. The city medical examiner's office said it was investigating the cause of Apa's death.

Her father told The New York Times that she had rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition in which muscles can break down during exertion, releasing substances that can poison the body. It was her first marathon, Steve Apa said.

Rachel Apa during the New York Marathon. (Supplied)

New York Road Runners, the nonprofit club that stages the race, said in a news release that a bystander administered CPR to Apa, and event medical staffers also performed CPR and used a defibrillator. Paramedics arrived and took her to a hospital but were unable to save her.

Apa, an industrial-technology product manager and former college field hockey player, had run to raise money for Parkinson's disease in honour of her grandfather.

"It's unfathomable," her father told The Times. He said his daughter had been in "perfect health".

Michaela Nicholas was watching the race, cheering on any runners whose names she could discern from their bibs, when Apa passed. Nicholas recalled on Tuesday, local time, that she called out a message of encouragement, then saw Apa collapse about 15 metres further along the route.

Nicholas, a hospital social worker, said she tried to comfort Apa while two other race spectators administered CPR.

"I just held Rachel's hand and talked to her and told her that she wasn't alone and that she's loved, and I prayed for her," Nicholas, a clinical social worker, said by phone.

The death occurred as the marathon marked 50 years in its five-borough format. Early editions of the race had been run only in Central Park. A record 61,000 runners reached the finish line.

Australia's Haftu Strintzos takes a giant step towards the LA28 Olympics with a top-five finish at the New York Marathon.

"We are deeply saddened by Rachel's passing following running in Sunday's race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends and the entire running community," New York Road Runners said in its statement.

As word of Apa's death spread on Tuesday, money poured into her "Parkinson's Champions" fundraising page, quickly exceeding her $4,000 goal. The fundraiser was sponsored by the Parkinson's Foundation.

On the page, Apa said her grandfather, who had Parkinson's disease and died in 2022, "taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement".

Apa worked for TE Connectivity, which makes various electrical components and electronics. The company was grappling with the news on Tuesday and expressed condolences. So did Bucknell University, where Apa graduated in 2024 with a degree in markets, innovation and design, and where she scored a total of 17 goals for the school's field hockey team.

USA Field Hockey, the sport's governing body, said on social media that "Rachel's impact on the sport and those around her will not be forgotten".
